topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: From Arrows to Spaces

sections.title: What is a Vector? (Visualizing Magnitude & Direction)
lecture_lines: Vectors are arrows with magnitude and direction.
Visualize them starting from the origin.
A bird flies from nest at origin.
animations: Draw vector V as an arrow from (0,0) to (3,2) in #FFD700.
Label point (3,2) and vector V in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Parallelogram Rule
lecture_lines: Place the second tail at the first head.
Form a parallelogram with these two vectors.
The diagonal is the sum of vectors.
Like a boat moving across a current.
animations: Draw vector A (boat) and vector B (river) in #FFD700 and #00CED1.
Slide vector B to start at head of vector A.
Draw parallelogram and diagonal resultant vector R in #FF4500.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching the Arrow
lecture_lines: Scaling stretches or shrinks a vector.
Multiplying by 3 triples the arrow length.
Negative scalars reverse the vector direction.
animations: Animate V scaling to 3V (length x3) and then to -1V (opposite direction).
Highlight the scalar multiplier changing dynamically.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Basis vectors 'i' and 'j' define the space.
Any 2D vector is a combination of them.
This grid movement is a linear combination.
animations: Display standard basis unit vectors i (1,0) and j (0,1) in #ADFF2F.
Show vector V decomposed into linear combination x*i + y*j.
Highlight the grid cells covered by these vectors.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Linear Transformations
lecture_lines: Transformations move, rotate, and resize spaces.
These operations form the basis of AI.
Like pinching to zoom on your screen.
animations: Display 2D grid of vectors representing a coordinate space.
Apply transformation matrix to stretch/rotate the grid visually.
Fade in 'Linear Transformations' text at top center.
